column1: # documentation/DOC_GATE_EMITTED_SURFACE_OPEN.tsv — GATE 89 (`emitted-surface`) adjudicated-open rows.
# Each row is a name the code EMITS — a JSON key printed by solve.c, or a whole-line KEY=value
# verdict token printed by solve.c or a scripts/*.sh gate — that appears in NO file under
# documentation/. These rows print [OPEN] and do NOT set GATE 89's exit code, so the gate is hard
# for NEWLY undocumented names only; a green verdict means no NEW one, never none at all.
# This began as the 2026-09-08 CENSUS taken when the gate landed: 230 rows, 160 JSON keys of the
# 362 emitted and 70 verdict tokens of the 114 then measured. It was a documentation backlog in
# which every row was a real defect — a reader who saw the name in the output had nowhere to look
# it up — and it must only ever SHRINK.
# DRAINED to 2 rows on 2026-09-08, in three lanes the same day: 118 names first, then the 112 that
# remained (60 verdict tokens into documentation/DEVELOPMENT.md, 4 solve.c tokens and 26 JSON
# certificate/atlas keys into documentation/SOLVE_C_CLI.md, and the 26 observability-sidecar keys
# into documentation/F1C5_LAYER_FORMAT.md).
# 🔴 THE TWO ROWS THAT REMAIN ARE NOT A BACKLOG. Both are names LEG 2 extracts that no run ever
# emits as a verdict — a self-test fixture literal and a line written into a generated stub
# harness that the gate then parses back. Each row's reason states the evidence. They are
# deliberately left undocumented rather than described in the reference tables, because
# publishing a token a reader can never see in a real log is worse than the gap it closes. If
# LEG 2 ever learns to tell a fixture from a verdict, both rows go.
# An allowance row that matches nothing FAILS: if the code stops emitting the name, or the name
# becomes documented, the row must be deleted. It therefore cannot outlive its fix, and it cannot
# be padded with names the code does not emit.
# 2026-09-08, LATER THE SAME DAY: GATE 89 grew LEG 3, an `ast` pass over solve.py, and solve.py's
# JSON surface stopped being scoped out. That census added 44 `py-json-key` rows, and THOSE 44 ARE
# A BACKLOG in the original sense — every one is a key a reader can see in bank.json, header.json,
# env.json, shard_<pool>_<n>.json, results.json, compute_stats.json, a --sat-encode .meta.json or a
# --branch-yield-report-json file with nothing in documentation/ to look it up in. They must only
# ever SHRINK, and they are counted separately, in DOC_GATE_EMITTED_SURFACE_PY_OPEN, so that
# draining them cannot be confused with movement on the two rows above.
# Columns (tab-separated): surface<TAB>name<TAB>site<TAB>reason
#   surface  json-key | verdict-token | py-json-key
#   name     the emitted identifier
#   site     for json-key/verdict-token, the first emission site at the 2026-09-08 census
#            (informational; not re-verified). For py-json-key, the emitting FUNCTION, the artifact
#            it is written into and the flag that writes it — symbols, never line numbers, which
#            go stale within the day.
#   reason   why the row stands
verdict-token
column4: NOT a runtime verdict and deliberately left undocumented: the only occurrence in the tree is a fixture literal inside scripts/tr12_repro_gate.sh --selftest-skip-pin, standing in for an arbitrary battery row while skip_pin_compare is red-tested. The real per-row tokens (TR12_Q7, TR12_XA_A, ...) are written dynamically via printf '%s=%s' and are invisible to LEG 2; no row named TR12_A exists in any VERDICTS.txt or in scripts/tr12_expected/n9/_EXPECTED_SKIPS.txt. Documenting it would publish a name no run emits.

column4: NOT a published verdict and deliberately left undocumented: emitted only into a stub harness that scripts/d5_04_q7_witnesses_gate.sh generates and then parses itself (sed -n 's/^WITNESSES=//p'), to read back TOKSTATE[TR12_Q7_WITNESSES] in the with-solver and without-solver worlds. It never reaches the gate's own caller; the gate's verdict token is D5_04_Q7_WITNESSES_GATE.
